definition: An AI agent's ability to detect that an action or plan has failed and adapt its approach accordingly, rather than repeating the same mistake or giving up entirely.
details: Robust failure recovery is essential for reliable agentic systems operating in real-world, imperfect environments where tool calls can fail, information can be incomplete, and initial plans may need revision.
story: Imagine handing a to-do list to a very clever intern who refuses to guess: before each step, they look around, check the result, and adjust. Boil it down and it is this: An AI agent's ability to detect that an action or plan has failed and adapt its approach accordingly, rather than repeating the same mistake or giving up entirely. Here is why it matters: Robust failure recovery is essential for reliable agentic systems operating in real-world, imperfect environments where tool calls can fail, information can be incomplete, and initial plans may need revision. The model stops being a one-shot answer machine and becomes a coworker that checks its own work. That loop of reason, act, and observe is Failure Recovery (in agents).
